verdicts.reason: A uses a sensible split for the landscape format, with a large product on the left and logo, headline and CTA on the right. But 'Glow' is tiny for the canvas and barely outranks the CTA, the right column has large uneven gaps, and the bottom-left corner of the product sits over the decorative circle. B has the same layout with a smaller product, which leaves more dead space in the middle and makes the composition feel weaker and less deliberate.

In A the product is small and its bottom-left corner overlaps the decorative circle. The right text column floats with big vertical gaps, and the headline is undersized. B moves the product to the right, so nothing collides, and it reads left to right from text to product. However, the product is still small, 'Glow' is weak, and there is a lot of empty space around both groups.

A is just a shrunk copy of the vertical stack, centred on the canvas. The product is tiny, its SOLSTICE label can't be read, and most of the landscape canvas is empty, so the layout doesn't fit the format. B rearranges into a proper two-column layout with a large product and a right-hand text column. It still has a small headline, loose vertical spacing, and a product corner overlapping the circle.

A has the product on the left and the text on the right. The product is a good size, but the headline is small, the column spacing is loose, and the product's corner overlaps the circle. B has a big product on the right and the text column on the left, but the CTA sits on top of the decorative circle and the left column is crammed into the corner. Its oversized product also overpowers the tiny 'Glow' headline.
